title: Remove Element
statement: Remove all instances of a given value in-place and return the new length.

mistakes.hint1: Try to do something like shifting elements to overwrite the ones you want to remove.
mistakes.hint2: Consider using two pointers: one to scan, one to place the safe elements.
mistakes.hint3: Think about how you would overwrite the target elements instead of creating a new array.
mistakes.hint4: Keep a `write_index` that only moves forward when you see a number different from the target value.

mistakes.hint1: Your counter seems to be adding up every time regardless of the value.
mistakes.hint2: Only increment the counter when the element is NOT the value to remove.
mistakes.hint3: Ensure your counter variable is placed *inside* the `if` block.
mistakes.hint4: The counter should represent the new length of the array without the removed values.

mistakes.hint2: Is your pointer correctly incrementing to reach the end of the array?
mistakes.hint3: Make sure you aren't accidentally decrementing your loop counter.
mistakes.hint4: Ensure your loop strictly advances `i < n` every iteration.

mistakes.hint1: How does your code behave if the array only has 1 element?
mistakes.hint2: Test your logic on an array of length 1. Does it work?
mistakes.hint3: Does it crash if n=1? Make sure loop bounds handle small inputs.

mistakes.hint1: What happens if the value to remove is completely absent from the array?
mistakes.hint2: If the array is [1, 2, 3] and target is 5, the length should stay 3.
mistakes.hint3: Does your code accidentally modify the array if the target isn't there?
mistakes.hint4: A correct two-pointer approach will simply overwrite the array with its own identical values, which is safe.

mistakes.hint1: What happens if every element in the array equals the value you need to remove?
mistakes.hint2: If the input is [2, 2, 2] and target is 2, your function should return 0.
mistakes.hint3: Trace your code. Does it correctly overwrite everything or leave a stray 2?
mistakes.hint4: Make sure your pointer strictly starts at 0 and doesn't advance unless it finds a safe element.

mistakes.hint1: Are you using `==` when you should be using `!=`?
mistakes.hint2: You only want to keep elements that do NOT match the target value.
mistakes.hint3: If you check `array[i] == val`, you are keeping the elements you are supposed to remove.
mistakes.hint4: Change your inner `if` condition to check for inequality (`!= val`).
